The workhorse of U.S. economic sanctions. After declaring a national emergency over an unusual and extraordinary threat that originates largely abroad, the President may block property and prohibit transactions involving foreign countries, entities, and individuals.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: 91 Stat. 1625](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/91/1625){.btn-official} [Current U.S. Code: 50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq.](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/50/1701?link-type=html){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Sec. 202: requires a declared national emergency specific to the threat.
- Sec. 203: power to investigate, block, regulate, or prohibit transactions and property subject to U.S. jurisdiction.
- Sec. 203(b): exceptions for personal communications, humanitarian donations, informational materials, and travel.
- Sec. 204: consultation with and reporting to Congress.
- Sec. 206: civil and criminal penalties, raised substantially in 2007.

## Why it matters

Almost every program administered by the Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control rests on it, each tied to an emergency under the [National Emergencies Act](nea-1976.qmd). Statutory sanctions such as the [Global Magnitsky Act](glomag-2016.qmd) and [CAATSA](caatsa-2017.qmd) are implemented through its machinery. After the 2026 tariff ruling, trade measures shifted to other authorities such as [Section 232](sec232-1962.qmd).

## Current status

In force. On February 20, 2026 the Supreme Court held 6 to 3 in Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump that the act does not authorize the President to impose tariffs. Its use for sanctions was not at issue.

[Last checked November 10, 2026.]{.checked}

## In the courts

- [Dames & Moore](../cases/dames-moore-1981.qmd) (1981). Held that IEEPA authorized the President to nullify attachments and order the transfer of Iranian assets.
- [Learning Resources v. Trump](../cases/learning-resources-2026.qmd) (2026). Held that the act's authority to regulate importation does not include the power to impose tariffs.

## Where it sits

- **Layer.** Framework statute. Standing laws that create institutions or general procedures other laws and executive actions plug into, such as the National Security Act, the War Powers Resolution, IEEPA, and FISA. ([How the layers work](../study/index.qmd#the-authority-stack))
- **Builds on.** [National Emergencies Act](nea-1976.qmd), [Trading with the Enemy Act](twea-1917.qmd).
- **Built upon by.** [USA PATRIOT Act](patriot-2001.qmd), [Global Magnitsky Act](glomag-2016.qmd), [CAATSA](caatsa-2017.qmd), [Export Control Reform Act](ecra-2018.qmd).
- **Codified in.** [Title 50 U.S.C.](title50-usc.qmd).
- **Era.** Vietnam, Watergate, and reassertion ([timeline](../study/timeline.qmd)).
- **Study.** [Unit 5: Emergency and economic powers](../study/units/emergencies-sanctions.qmd) (core reading).
- **Who's involved.** [HFAC](../whos-who.qmd#hfac), [Senate Banking](../whos-who.qmd#senate-banking), [OFAC](../whos-who.qmd#ofac).

## Connections

| This statute | Other statute | Note |
|---|---|---|
| relies on | [National Emergencies Act](nea-1976.qmd){.subj} | IEEPA powers can be used only after an emergency is declared under the NEA. |
| succeeds | [Trading with the Enemy Act](twea-1917.qmd){.subj} | Took over the peacetime emergency powers of TWEA Sec. 5(b). |
| related to | [UN Participation Act](unpa-1945.qmd){.subj} | UNPA Sec. 5 is a parallel authority for implementing U.N. sanctions. |
| amended by | [USA PATRIOT Act](patriot-2001.qmd){.subj} | Allowed blocking of assets during the pendency of an investigation. |
| related to | [AEDPA (terrorism)](aedpa-1996.qmd){.subj} | Terrorist organization designations run in parallel with IEEPA terrorism sanctions. |
| relied on by | [Global Magnitsky Act](glomag-2016.qmd){.subj} | Implemented through Executive Order 13818 using IEEPA blocking authority. |
| relied on by | [CAATSA](caatsa-2017.qmd){.subj} | Sanctions are imposed using IEEPA authorities. |
| related to | [Iran Sanctions Act](iran-sanctions-1996.qmd){.subj} | Statutory sanctions layered on top of the IEEPA Iran emergency. |
| succeeded by | [Export Control Reform Act](ecra-2018.qmd){.subj} | Ended reliance on IEEPA emergencies to keep export controls in force. |
| related to | [Section 232 (trade)](sec232-1962.qmd){.subj} | Alternative tariff authority after the 2026 ruling that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs. |
